import sys

def f(s):
    # convert to list for mutable operations
    s = list(s)
    n = len(s)

    # first loop: replace first "at" (not at index 0) with "@"
    i = 1
    while i < n - 2:
        if s[i] == 'a' and s[i+1] == 't':
            # replace two characters with one '@'
            s[i:i+2] = ['@']
            n = len(s)
            break
        i += 1

    # second loop: replace "dot" with "." (only starting from index 1 up to n-4)
    i = 1
    while i < n - 3:
        if s[i] == 'd' and s[i+1] == 'o' and s[i+2] == 't':
            # replace three characters with one '.'
            s[i:i+3] = ['.']
            n = len(s)
            # i is incremented at the end of the loop body, as in C++ for loop
        i += 1

    return ''.join(s)

def main():
    # read all whitespace-separated tokens (matches cin >> s)
    for token in sys.stdin.read().split():
        print(f(token))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
